scope: evidence-first daily materiality filter; no production writes
significance: One new upstream change modifies the Three.js research benchmark; one retrospective Blender documentation correction narrows the asset-reload experiment. No production promotion or priority reordering.

findings.materiality: New upstream evidence separates JS-side shader construction cost from GPU pipeline compilation and can change the design of the existing renderer benchmark.
findings.source_quality: A for merged Three.js implementation/PR diff; B for author-supplied synthetic benchmark; no measurement on our scenes
findings.evidence: In TSL function layouts nested includes previously regenerated for each call path. Merged change deduplicates by builder/stage, provides optional parameter handling, and adds test cases. Author reports 682 -> 33 FunctionNode.generate calls in an all-MaterialX-noises shader, and depth-12 nested-layout shader-build work 3.87ms -> 0.40ms. Author states generated shaders are byte-identical for the tested configuration.
contradictions_and_limits: The 3.87 to 0.40ms gain is CPU-side build time for a specific nested-layout stress test, NOT a GPU frame-time, shader-driver compile, or KONA load-time result.
Current main code searches in konam, bellagio and studio-kona show no explicit WebGPURenderer or THREE.TSL usage; immediate production benefit is unproven.
Optimized code is in Three.js dev/r187 milestone, not proof that a stable released renderer includes it.
findings.engineering: Revise EXP-THREE-R187-001 to benchmark CPU TSL graph-generation time, generated shader identity/size, GPU pipeline compile time, warm/cold first-frame latency, correctness, and mobile behavior separately. Include synthetic deep nested layouts and a real Bellagio/KONA material only after isolating them in a research harness. Never infer FPS gain from shader-build microbenchmarks.

findings.materiality: Corrects an over-broad assumption in the existing externally reloaded collection experiment before it is specified around unsupported direct GLB collection importing.
findings.source_quality: A: official Blender 5.3 Pipeline & I/O developer release notes
findings.evidence: Blender's Collection Importer currently supports USD only. It can store import settings on collections in .blend projects, and reload/clear/make-local operations were added, but this does not establish glTF/GLB collection-import reload support.
contradictions_and_limits: glTF import and export functionality exists separately in Blender; 'USD-only collection importer' does not imply Blender cannot import GLB.
Blender 5.3 is development/release-note track as of this date; do not infer stable production maturity.
The 2026-10-10 evidence report described collection reload generically; it did not demonstrate a GLB reload round trip.
findings.engineering: Amend EXP-BLENDER-ASSET-AS-CODE-001: use USD for native linked/reloaded Collection Importer cases; treat glTF/GLB export as a separate browser-delivery round-trip; record source format, collection asset identity and transform, mapping to GLB semantic IDs, edit conflict policy, and rebuild determinism. No central source-authority migration.

watch_only.reason: Confirmed fix for shared TextureSource among multi-render-target attachments. Code inspection of konam and bellagio main found WebGLRenderTarget for postprocessing but no multi-attachment count, so project incidence not established. Add MRT case only if planned hybrid renderer uses multiple attachments.
WebGPU canvas target GPU depth/color resource disposal now explicit; no current WebGPU use in searched main branches, so no new isolated experiment.
KHR_interactivity clarified interpolation rejects ref types; semantic room interactions remain runtime-owned, so no architecture change.
KHR_materials_retroreflection is only release candidate; promising for night cycling/high-vis visuals, but no validated project need or browser support. Retrospective, not a new October 13 event.
